Tanzania is home to some of the best national parks in Tanzania — and in Africa. From the endless plains of the Serengeti to the volcanic walls of the Ngorongoro Crater, this East African country packs more wildlife density per square kilometer than almost anywhere else on earth. If you are planning a Tanzania safari, choosing the right parks can make or break your trip.

In this guide, we break down the top Tanzania safari parks, what makes each one unique, the best time to visit, and how to combine them into one unforgettable itinerary.

Why Tanzania Is a Top Safari Destination

Tanzania protects nearly a third of its total land area for wildlife conservation. That commitment has created a network of parks and reserves that host the Great Migration in Tanzania, the Big Five, and some of the highest lion and elephant densities on the continent. Whether you want open-plains game drives, crater floors packed with predators, or tree-climbing lions, Tanzania’s parks deliver.

Quick Facts: Tanzania’s Protected Areas
  • Tanzania has 22 national parks and dozens of game and forest reserves
  • The Serengeti-Ngorongoro ecosystem covers over 30,000 square kilometers
  • Tanzania hosts roughly 20% of Africa’s large mammal population
  • The Great Migration involves over 1.5 million wildebeest and 250,000 zebras

1. Serengeti National Park

No list of the best national parks in Tanzania is complete without the Serengeti. Its endless golden plains are the stage for the Great Migration, where wildebeest and zebra move in a continuous, predictable circuit chasing rain and fresh grass. Big cat sightings are almost guaranteed here, with healthy populations of lion, leopard, and cheetah.

Best time to visit: June to October for the northern migration and river crossings; December to March for calving season in the southern plains.

2. Ngorongoro Crater

The Ngorongoro Crater is the world’s largest intact volcanic caldera and one of the most reliable places on earth to see the Big Five in a single day. Roughly 25,000 large animals live within its walls year-round, including one of Tanzania’s last free-roaming black rhino populations.

Best time to visit: Year-round, since resident wildlife rarely leaves the crater floor.

3. Tarangire National Park

Tarangire National Park is famous for its ancient baobab trees and the largest elephant herds in Tanzania. During the dry season, the Tarangire River becomes a lifeline, drawing enormous concentrations of elephant, buffalo, and plains game.

Best time to visit: June to October, when animals gather along the river.

Did You Know?

Tarangire National Park has one of the highest elephant densities in East Africa, with herds of up to 300 individuals recorded during peak dry season.

4. Lake Manyara National Park

Lake Manyara National Park is compact but diverse, combining groundwater forest, acacia woodland, and an alkaline lake that attracts thousands of flamingos. It is best known for its tree-climbing lions and excellent birdwatching, making it a popular first or last stop on a Tanzania safari circuit.

Best time to visit: November to June for birdlife and lush scenery.

5. Ruaha National Park

Ruaha is Tanzania’s largest national park and one of its most underrated. Located in the south, it offers a wilder, less-crowded safari experience with large predator populations, including one of Africa’s biggest lion prides recorded in a single park.

Best time to visit: June to October for concentrated game viewing along the Great Ruaha River.

6. Nyerere National Park (Selous)

Formerly part of the Selous Game Reserve, Nyerere National Park is a vast wilderness crossed by the Rufiji River. It is one of the few parks where walking safaris and boat safaris are widely available, adding variety beyond the standard game drive.

Best time to visit: June to October, during the dry season.

Combining Tanzania’s Parks with a Zanzibar Beach Extension

Many travelers pair their Tanzania safari with a few days on the beaches of Zanzibar. After several days of early morning game drives across the Serengeti or Ngorongoro Crater, the white sand and turquoise water of Zanzibar make an easy, low-effort way to end the trip. Flights between Arusha or Kilimanjaro and Zanzibar are short, so it is simple to add a 3–4 day beach stay onto any northern circuit safari without losing park time.

How to Choose Between Tanzania’s National Parks

Most travelers do not choose just one park — they combine two or three into a single circuit. A classic first-timer route pairs the Serengeti and Ngorongoro Crater with Tarangire or Lake Manyara for a mix of migration drama, crater game viewing, and elephant encounters. Travelers wanting a quieter, less-touristed experience often add Ruaha or Nyerere National Park to their Tanzania safari packages.

Consider these factors when planning:

  • Time of year: Migration timing shifts each year, so align your dates with river crossings or calving season if that is your priority.
  • Trip length: A 5–7 day safari comfortably covers the northern circuit; 10+ days allows the southern parks too.
  • Travel style: Walking and boat safaris are best in the south; classic 4×4 game drives dominate the north.
  • Budget: Northern parks tend to be pricier and busier; southern parks offer more exclusivity for a similar wildlife experience.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the best national park to visit in Tanzania?

The Serengeti National Park is widely considered the best national park in Tanzania because of its size, predator density, and role in the Great Migration.

How many national parks does Tanzania have?

Tanzania has 22 official national parks, alongside game reserves and conservation areas such as the Ngorongoro Conservation Area.

What is the best time of year for a Tanzania safari?

The dry season from June to October offers the best game viewing across most parks, while December to March is ideal for the calving season in the southern Serengeti.

Can I visit the Serengeti and Ngorongoro Crater in one trip?

Yes. The Serengeti and Ngorongoro Crater sit within the same ecosystem and are commonly combined into a single 5–7 day safari itinerary.

Common Mistakes to Avoid When Planning a Tanzania Safari

Even experienced travelers make avoidable mistakes when booking a Tanzania safari. Trying to fit too many parks into too few days often means more time driving between gates than actually watching wildlife. Booking during peak migration months without confirming lodge availability months in advance can also mean missing out on the best-located camps. Finally, skipping a local safari planner in favor of a generic online itinerary can leave out seasonal details, such as which side of the Serengeti the migration is likely to be on during your travel dates.
